title: Audience, sponsor and decision authority
objective: What do you do if only the champion attends the planned executive readout?.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: The right audience turns a presentation into a decision. Confirm who will be in the room and what each person can decide.

items: **The executive sponsor:** confirms priority, investment support, and next-step authority.
**The champion:** explains the work and adds customer credibility.
**The technical champion:** validates dependencies and the evaluation plan.
**Key participants from DITL:** department heads and front-line employees who can speak to the workflows firsthand.
**The AE and SE owners**, plus a Glean sales leader if necessary.

blocks.x: Don't assume an enthusiastic end user, or even a champion, is the economic buyer. Confirm the actual decision process. Separate three things:

items: **Sponsorship:** support for the initiative and its resources.
**Signature and procurement authority:** the paper process.

blocks.x: These may be different people, so record each one.

If only the champion attends, use the meeting to prepare and refine the case, and then secure the sponsor's decision in a separate meeting. Don't log executive alignment as confirmed when it didn't happen.
Sponsorship, budget authority, and signature authority often sit with different people. Name each one.

blocks.title: Three kinds of authority
blocks.alt: Three stacked kinds of authority that often sit with different people: sponsorship, which backs the priority; budget authority, which funds it; and signature and procurement authority, which commits the organization.

items.label: Sponsorship
items.detail: Backs the priority above the champion

items.label: Budget authority
items.detail: Holds or can shift the budget

practice.x: Your planned executive readout is attended only by the champion. What do you do?

worked.x: Use the time well. Walk the champion through the case, test the assumptions, and ask what the sponsor will challenge. Agree how the champion will help secure a 30-minute decision meeting with the sponsor this week or next.
Record the session as "preparation with the champion," not "executive alignment," and update the mutual action plan with the new decision date.
